statusText: Mapped policy state: EA_ON. Tail risk is low at 13% while Stress stays elevated at 53%; the Nasdaq-100 continues to trade a genuinely two-sided monthly-expiry Friday against a long end near 20-month yield highs.
recommendation: Conditions remain consistent with functioning mean reversion: the session has produced a full round trip, both extremes have been retraced, price sits mid-range in cash and futures, and implied volatility is at session lows. A narrow evidence-based caution window is carried at 19:00Z-20:00Z, where August monthly options expiry concentrates closing and roll flow into the cash close, and it releases at that close. Existing-position management and emergency protection are unaffected by this assessment.
headline: Mid-range into expiry: the Nasdaq-100 has retraced both of today's extremes and sits below its open, with VIX at session lows against a 4.74% 10-year.
body:
Cash NDX trades near 29,313.54, about +0.34% on the day. The index opened at 29,359.60, was sold to a 29,142.44 low, reclaimed the whole decline to a 29,405.12 high and has since handed back roughly ninety points to trade below its own open; NQ September futures are near 29,372.50, about +0.25%, inside a 29,220.00-29,539.00 range against a 29,300.50 prior close and some 166 points below their session high. That sequence remains the central Tail evidence. Both extremes have been retraced, neither has produced repeated extension after a failed pullback, and price is sitting in the middle of its range rather than pinned near an edge, which is the opposite of the persistent no-retracement path that overwhelms mean reversion. Volatility agrees: VIX is 14.89, down 6.0% on the day and near the bottom of a 14.77-15.95 range.

The stress side of the ledger remains genuinely elevated and is almost entirely a rates and fiscal story. The 10-year yield is 4.74%, testing the 20-month highs set earlier in the week, with the 2-year at 4.24% and the 30-year at 5.28%. Reporting today notes the long end has given back almost all of the relief that followed the Treasury's decision to at least double buybacks of long-dated debt, an operation that only begins on September 9, with strategists doubting it can offset rate expectations or Fed-credibility concerns. Gold at roughly 4,627 dollars, up about 2.5% and at its highest since mid-May after the national debt reached a record 40 trillion dollars this week, is the clearest cross-asset expression of that same fiscal concern. WTI near 87 dollars, heading for a second consecutive weekly gain of about 5% on supply disruption, keeps an inflation input under the long end.

Today's macro is already behind the market. The S&P Global flash PMIs printed at 13:45Z with services at 56.8, the composite at 56.0 and manufacturing at 53.2 against a 53.9 consensus, the strongest output growth in more than four years and precisely the growth strength that keeps yields heavy. Price discovery since the release has been orderly and two-sided, which matters more here than the surprise itself. Internals are split rather than aligned: on a latest-session basis megacaps are five up and three down, led by TSLA, GOOGL and META against weakness in AAPL, AMZN and NVDA, while the semiconductor complex is marginally lower. That conflict reduces directional conviction and lifts Stress; under this framework it does not lift Tail.

The one narrow forward checkpoint inside the live horizon is August monthly options expiry, which concentrates closing and roll flow into the 20:00Z cash close. A caution window is carried at 19:00Z-20:00Z on that basis alone, as a scheduled-flow checkpoint rather than an observed structure, and it releases at the close. From 21:00Z CME equity index futures halt for the weekend, so every later published hour describes a market with no tradable path rather than a forecast of benign structure. A reported US-Canada tariff deadline tonight lands inside that halt and is therefore carried as reopen gap risk. Next week's asymmetry sits on Wednesday, where Core PCE, the second-estimate GDP print and NVIDIA results land in one session, ahead of the Jackson Hole keynote on Friday.

lookbackSummary: Claude coverage over the past 24 hours is partial: eleven hourly assessments are available (01:00Z, 06:00Z, 07:00Z, 08:00Z and 11:00Z through 17:00Z) while the remaining thirteen clock-hours, covering the whole of the August 20 US afternoon and evening plus scattered overnight gaps, have no published assessment and are marked unavailable. Across the available hours the published Tail held a narrow 12-16 band and the mapped policy state was green throughout. The shape is informative: Tail sat at 12 through the Asian and European hours with Stress easing from 59 to 54 as the overnight tape stayed orderly, then stepped up to 15-16 across the 13:00Z-14:00Z flash-PMI and US-open window, where the dominant mode was briefly published as event/whipsaw. Since the release Tail has come back down through 14 to 13 and held there for three consecutive hours while the mode returned to mixed, which is the signature of an event absorbed rather than one that started a trend. Confidence improved steadily from 83 to 88 as live cash, futures, volatility and rate evidence became available through the European and US mornings.
outlookSummary: The forecast holds the current hour at a low Tail while the observed two-way structure continues to be confirmed, then carries one watch-level hour at 19:00Z where August monthly options expiry concentrates closing and roll flow into the 20:00Z cash close; that elevation is a scheduled-flow checkpoint rather than an observed structure and it releases immediately afterwards. From 21:00Z the published horizon changes character entirely: CME equity index futures halt for the weekend, so every subsequent slot describes a market with no tradable price path. Tail falls into the low single digits there because the pathological path this score measures requires a live market, and Stress steps down to a floor that represents the standing rate and fiscal backdrop rather than a live condition. Confidence decays gradually across the weekend with distance from the last observed print rather than because the evidence gathered deteriorated. Weekend headline risk, including a reported US-Canada tariff deadline tonight and continuing energy-supply developments, is carried as reopen gap risk for the Sunday 22:00Z restart, which lies beyond this horizon, and next week's concentration of Core PCE, second-estimate GDP and NVIDIA results on Wednesday, Treasury note supply from Tuesday to Thursday and Friday's Jackson Hole keynote is treated as a forward Stress and dispersion consideration only.
